title: Returning home after his father's death and passing on Glenn Miller
summary: He gave up an offer from Irving Aronson and a Glenn Miller recommendation to come home when his father died in 1939.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Joe Marcella, yeah. Joe had the band at the Hickory House then. I think it was for business reasons, you know, trying to get himself up a little bit. And we even roomed together. Sharky and I lived together. But he used somebody else on clarinet, Joe Marcella, most of the time I think. And we played at Knicks and then we played at the Yacht Club on 52nd Street, at the Village Barn, quite a few places around there. And then my father died and so I decided to come home, try to make the funeral now. I missed it incidentally. And just around that time Irving Aronson had a staff band, which was at WGN I believe, and he offered me to come to work with him playing third alto and jazz clarinet. And Fazola at the same time quit Glenn Miller to go with Bob Crosby. So Fazola recommended me to go with Glenn Miller. So Eddie Miller was in town at the time and he recommended me to Glenn Miller and I was supposed to go to rehearsal. And I had to call him off, call him up and tell him I was off because I was coming home. And Irving Aronson told me if I came back within three months the job was still open for me. But I never did get back until last year I went there just for a couple of weeks for a vacation trip.
